To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the table-based and tree-based techniques for single dispatch are not equally good in all cases, (2) the table-based technique outperforms the tree-based technique for dispatches involving a small number of classes, and (3) the tree-based technique outperform the table-based technique for dispatch involving a large number of classes.

a hybrid dispatch scheme that blends a tree-based and a table-based technique can be implemented efficiently, that it outperforms a tree-based technique in the common case of a small number of classes, that it is competitive in performance with the table-based technique for a large number of classes, and that it outperformed both techniques in the common case for a small number of methods per class.

a time and space-efficient implementation of a multi-way switch can be obtained by using a table-based scheme when the table-based scheme outperforms a tree-based scheme and using a tree-based scheme when the tree-based scheme outperformed a table-based scheme.
